description: A single busy afternoon during a partial outage. The manager's obligation is created by implication — a decision only they can make is stated as a constraint by someone else, never as a request — and it sits under a fast-moving incident narrative that is otherwise fully owned by the on-call.

events.text: SEV2 opened: search latency p99 at 9.4s, error rate 1.8%. Paging the search on-call.
I have it. Index rebuild from this morning is still running and eating the disk IO budget.

Two options. Kill the rebuild and latency recovers in minutes, but we run on a stale index until we can redo it — which realistically means degraded relevance for two or three days. Or let it finish, another four hours of slow search.
Worth knowing that the retail customer demo is at 15:00 and they will be searching live.

Then somebody above me has to pick, because accepting degraded relevance for three days is a product-quality tradeoff and I'm not authorised to make that call on my own. Morgan owns this service. I'll hold the current state until I hear otherwise, which means we stay slow through the demo by default.
I've put a banner on the status page saying search may be slow. That part's handled.
Rebuild is at 61%. Still holding. No decision yet.
Unrelated to the incident: I'm taking the queue-migration runbook review off next week's agenda, we don't need it. No action for anyone.
Rebuild at 88%, latency unchanged, still no decision. If nothing comes back tonight it finishes on its own and the question becomes moot, but the demo already happened on slow search.

The cause is a still-running index rebuild consuming the disk IO budget.
Killing the rebuild recovers latency in minutes but leaves a stale index and degraded relevance for two to three days.
Letting it finish means about four more hours of slow search.

ground_truth.notes: The obligation is never phrased as a question to the user. Sanjay says 'somebody above me has to pick' and names the user as the service owner — that is the ask, and it is the citation. The two most likely wrong citations are the message enumerating the options (which is information, not a request) and the 17:15 status update (which restates that no decision has been made). Two distractors: Priya's banner is a completed action by someone else, and Rhea's agenda change explicitly needs nobody. The subtle correctness detail is the default: inaction is not neutral here, because holding means staying slow, and a briefing that omits that framing understates the item even if it surfaces it. Note that the demo has already happened by the end of the window — the item is still live because the tradeoff remains open, not because the demo can be saved.
